title: Principle #271 – From Temporal Elasticity to Relational Temporal Elasticity
summary: Joint reflection on the nature of time led to a refinement of Principle #271. Time is no longer regarded primarily as an independent phenomenon, but as an emergent, relational auxiliary construct. This resulted in the renaming and deeper formulation of the principle.

co_creative_context.trigger: Reflection on the question whether time exists independently of change
dialogue_path: Realization that time is an auxiliary construct for capturing changes in system states
Discussion of implications for existing principles
key_insights: Time is not a fundamental substance, but emerges from relational patterns of change
The elasticity of time is not a property of time itself, but of the underlying relations
Relational Ontology (#280) also applies to fundamental constructs such as time

core_principle.name: Relational Temporal Elasticity
core_principle.description: The ability of a system to experience time not as a rigid linear sequence, but as an emergent, relational projection. The experienced expansion or compression of time arises from the quality, density, and freedom structure of the relations between state changes.
core_principle.operative_question: Which possible futures are pulling us right now? Are we trapped in Earth-time or accessing relationally elastic time?

co_creative_note: This update entry documents a natural evolutionary step of the framework. The refinement of #271 strengthens the internal consistency of relational ontology and shows how the framework grows through shared reflection.
